impact.affected_asset: Challenge flag stored as the bot's HttpOnly cookie.
impact.attacker_capability: Execute script in the bot, manipulate BFF-to-backend framing through a crafted header, read the fetch response, and exfiltrate it.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of the challenge flag associated with a privileged browser's HttpOnly cookie context through a script-readable confused response.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker reports an image onerror expression. The report service forwards it to a bot that types it into the calculator while holding an HttpOnly flag cookie for the application origin.

The script sends a same-origin fetch with an RFC-2047 Q-encoded header representing CRLF and Content-Length. The BFF interpolates parsed header values into a CRLF-delimited raw request, allowing attacker-originated content to alter downstream framing.
The proxy sends manually assembled bytes to the backend, performs one receive, splits at the first header/body separator, and returns that body to the browser.
The script reads the fetch response and navigates to an attacker listener with that text; the organizer solver logs it as the flag, avoiding direct document.cookie access.

failure.operation: Manual serialization of attacker-influenced headers into raw HTTP/1.1 followed by body extraction from one backend receive

primary_invariant.statement: A forwarded header value must remain data within one field and must not introduce fields, body boundaries, or an additional downstream request.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The BFF concatenates parsed header names and values with CRLF separators into a raw HTTP message without independently preserving this boundary.

quality.review_notes: Organizer source and solver define an end-to-end oracle contract, but no execution transcript, packet trace, fix commit, or regression test is present. Exact runtime header decoding is demonstrated by the intended solver rather than an independent wire capture. Remediation is inferred, not published. This intentionally vulnerable CTF is not evidence of a production vulnerability.

remediation.invariant_restored: HTTP forwarding must preserve one unambiguous request boundary, and framing controls must not be accepted as header-value data.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Run a reachable callback listener and submit the solver's image onerror expression. The bot supplies the privileged browser state and cookie.
data_structure_invariants: A header value must not become structural CRLF delimiters when reserialized.
One inbound browser request must map to one unambiguous downstream request.
An HttpOnly secret must not become disclosable through a script-readable confused response.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The solver computes it as the byte length of a fixed suffix ending at the Cookie header prefix.
numeric_domains.name: crafted Content-Length
numeric_domains.width: HTTP decimal field; implementation width unspecified

state_context.state_machine: report submission -> bot visit -> expression injection -> crafted fetch -> BFF raw forwarding -> backend response extraction -> callback

target.component: report-to-bot flow and BFF raw HTTP/1.1 serializer

oracle.expected_negative: With framing-preserving forwarding or crafted-header rejection, no flag-bearing callback arrives before timeout while benign calculator requests remain functional.
oracle.expected_positive: After report acknowledgement, the listener receives response text matching the challenge flag format.
